review_text: We were lucky enough to be the only 2 people booked for this 2-hour bike ride so Jenni was able to go at our pace. I had been a bit nervous of cycling amidst the Santiago traffic but needn't have worried - the route took us through a few quiet streets around Patio Bellavista but mostly through parks and alongside the river on dedicated cycle paths. It was great to have a guide to not only give you interesting information about the city but to show you the etiquette of crossing roads and pedestrian paths. The city has made a lot of effort to provide miles of cycle routes which interconnect safely. We had already spent a week in the city and seen a lot but the ride gave us access to places we would just not have found and provided a great way to see the Parques Metropolitano & Bicentenario. It was a great joy to be riding through beautiful green spaces with no responsibility to find the way home! The bikes were good, Jenni was warm and friendly and we had a great time. review_text: So, not wanting to be outdone by my brother who also did star gazing in San Pedro de Atacama, I had to do this too. I booked with Jorge, all very straight forward, you get all the information on what tours, prices, nights etc they will take place for you to choose. You pay once you get dropped back off at your hotel. The night itself… Jorge explains everything you need to know about the stars, basically like the Bill Bryson books “a short history on stars”. He made it fun and entertaining, asked questions to make sure you were listening (remember this part), then onto the telescopes! He had I think 9 or 10 pointed at different stars, planets and it was very much a wow factor, I am not an astronomer in any way or form but I loved this. It reminded me of just how much is unknown and out there. Very much worth the tour. Jorge’s family were there too and very much to my surprise there was food and drinks to be served near the end. The food were some hot and cold and drink very much the same… soup, tea etc and for those who like a little tipple at night … plenty to tempt you. Photos were taken afterwards of the sky as a group and individuals or whoever you came with. I would highly recommend him… oh, nearly forgot… for those who feel the cold, he had blankets on each chair and if you needed he also had heaters. It does get cold at night and as you are sitting and not moving around the cold sets in easily… wrap up well and enjoy!

review_text: Whilst most consider the park to be closed after April, it is open all year round. Moreover, the parc is absolutely beautiful at this time of the year (wonderful array of autumn colours - red, orange, yellow, green and white of course with the snowy mountains) and you can have it all to yourself (we saw nobody on our day and night trek on the 13th of May). Whilst most hotels and all 'refugios' are closed, one can still find places in May within the parc, stay in Puerto Natales (nice spot for some excellent food at the Afrigonia for instance) and also do what we did by having a fantastic day and night out with the Puma expert of Torres del Paine: Tomislav Goic. He is the guide with the most experience (has been a guide since 1978 in TdP), has so much knowledge of the TdP and has excellent energy and language skills (speaks English, French, Italian, Croatian and Spanish of course). He took my family and me out on a day trek and then a night search for Pumas and we had a wonderful time with him with exceptional views of the TdP late at night (exceptional lighting with a full moon) and early in the morning (magical). As he has been a guide here for so long, he organized for us to sleep in the guide lodge just at the entrance of the park - a very traditional treat in an old house that Tomi did so well to warm up for us. review_text: Lots of Chileans come here for summer vacation. There are camping and hostel type accommodations as wells as a couple of expensive hotels. There are some attractive restaurants serving ostiones or scallops. There are several kiosks with rocks and jewelry for sale. A very tie-dye atmosphere. Can be foggy and cold in the fall and winter months. There are kayak rentals as well as day trips to some petroglyphs and a national park. It makes a good break from the desert. Bring cash as there are no ATM's or banks except at the gas station and the next town, Caldera. Taxi fare to Caldera is 900 pesos .

review_text: When my friend and I booked our trip to the Atacama Desert, we were really excited to do some stargazing - only I made a big error when booking the trip, and put us too close to a full moon! We managed to rearrange our dates but then only had a small window to do stargazing (most tour operators do not do tours 3 days before and after a full moon because it's so bright). I emailed Jorge and asked of his availability, and he promptly messaged me back with information about his SAT 2 experience. Because of the positioning of the moon, Jorge picked my friend and me up at 1:50 AM (!) to start our experience at 2 AM at his place just outside of San Pedro de Atacama. There were at least 8 telescopes set up, and some seats with blankets and heat warmers (it was extremely cold! Bring layers!). Jorge grounded our group's understanding of the night sky with common terminology and a historical overview of the field of astronomy. Even though I was quite tired at the start of the experience, Jorge's humor and energy kept me wide awake and eager to learn more from him. After his lecture, we had a break for snacks, which included a generous spread of sandwiches, cookies, chips and dip, and hot beverages (and a very delicious asparagus soup). For the rest of our tour, it was impossible not to latch onto Jorge's enthusiasm about the stars. We watched the Milky Way and some constellations come and go, saw the rings of Saturn, and gazed into various galaxies. Jorge patiently answered all our questions, whether it was about the night sky or the physics and chemistry behind the stars. No question was too small for him. I was especially impressed after learning how he got into astronomy and how much he taught himself about the night sky. I've seen some clear and beautiful night skies before, but this was breathtaking, and I felt extremely fortunate to have had Jorge guide me through what bright dot in the sky was what. Sure, the tour isn't the cheapest in town, but you definitely are out in the field with a top-notch expert. I'd say that this is THE stargazing experience to be had in Atacama. Thank you Jorge for such an incredible and memorable evening with the stars!

review_text: We used Personal Tours Chile twice recently. Luis picked us up at the Santiago airport and transferred us to our hotel. He returned emails promptly and several days before our flight, he phoned us in Canada using What's App to ensure that we knew where we would meet up with him in the airport. We met with him exactly as described. A few days later, he picked us up at our hotel and gave us an all-day tour and transfer to the port of San Antonio. Several weeks before our trip, Luis had contacted us for the address of our hotel in San Antonio so he could program it into his GPS and know where he was going. On the morning of the tour, he got delayed by traffic but contacted us by What's App and kept us informed. Luis took us along the back roads to the Loma Larga Winery in the Casablanca Valley. At that time, we were the only ones at the winery so we received a wonderful private tour from Irene. We went for lunch in Casablanca at a typical Chilean restaurant. We then traveled to the coast, stopping to see wetlands and beaches. He was willing to stop wherever we wanted along the way. Once we got to San Antonio, he dropped us off at the hotel and insisted on accompanying us to make sure that we got checked in okay. His English was excellent; he was a safe driver, and was very friendly and easy to talk to.

review_text: We booked a 1/2 day kayak trip for 2 to La Poza. We were picked up on time by Jass who was friendly and welcoming as others have stated, We were dropped off at the location to meet our guide, and then began our brief training on the kayaks. We were 2, and considered ourselves beginners. The only kayak available to us when we made the reservation was the 2-person kayak. It was a very rainy and windy day and our little experience, combined with the untenable conditions and the brief training made the experience just average. I would suggest to beginners to seriously consider weather conditions before deciding to do something like this as our day was cut short unexpectedly and for the price you pay, you want to make sure you are getting what you paid for. Overall though, Jass was a responsible and attentive business person who does make sure to attend to questions and concerns both before and after the trip. We did our best to provide a pleasant experience by providing top quality equipment, an extremely qualified bilingual guide to help on your trip, we arrived on time, provided quality transport and gave an overall good service on our part. review_text: I am not giving three stars because the product is bad, I am giving three starts because it was too crowded and felt like mass tourism which is not my thing, and I hope my review helps people to decide. It was arguably the least remarkable of my excursions and adventures in Chillean Patagonia, but it had some aspects I enjoyed. Originally I had booked with a small operator who use a small and fast boat for more adventurous excursions which includes the Balmaceda glacier and other more exclusive locations, but unfortunately they cancelled because of minimum number of participants not reached. They Kindly proposed to rebook me on the trip to the Balmaceda glacier of Turismo 21 de Mayo, and I took the offer. I was punctually picked up at my hotel, and as the bus got full during more hotel stops I already knew that this would be a very busy trip. When we arrived at the dock I saw three more busses on the quay. They surely wouldn't all be on the same boat....? Yes they were, and most of them were tour groups. Below deck it felt like being crammed into a chicken pen, the 130 passenger boat was full to the brim and everybody was exitedly chatting and cackling on top of their voice. Definitely a great and positive atmosphere, but not something I'd enjoy for a full day! Luckily we were allowed to go outside after the boat sailed of, and only a hand full of people stayed there because of the cold and the wind, the rest disappeared below deck swiftly. I enjoyed the scenery on the way to the glacier very much. Beautiful light, a colony of cormorants, a spectacular waterfall spraying in the wind, and magnificent fjord and glacier landscape unfolding in front of the boat. They stopped the boat at points of interest, which allowed for time to have good looks and take photo's. Then the boat drops you off at land and you can walk to the glacier viewpoint. If you're a fast walker try to get off the boat first or you'll be as slow as the slowest person in front of you (Up to 130 persons, remember). Then at the viewpoint surely nice views, but I found it a bit underwhelming compared to other glaciers Ive seen in Patagonia. There was some pushing and shoving to take photos and selfies. Somebody accidentally knocked the lens cap of my camera without apologising, then a bit more crowd hassles, and back to the boat...that was it! Then onwards on the boat to the lunch stop at an estancia in a lovely location. The lunch was good, but the service was slowish and it took well over 2 hours. I wished I had the time to walk around and explore a bit around the estancia. maybe they should offer a quick lunch option to people who want to explore? Then back on the boat to Puerto Natales, again outside on the deck to avoid the crowds downstairs. And back to the hotel in a bus. Well organised, well executed, lovely staff, but a bit too much of a mass tourism thing to my tastes. And the crowdedness of it all caused moments which I experienced as awkward and unpleasant. I have noticed they also have smaller boats, and more exclusive trips, so please inquire. But on that day they crammed everyone on their biggest boat, which seemed to be the only one going there. I added some photo's of the lovely scenery, which was undeniably amazing!
title: The Balmaceda trip is not bad, but it is a very crowded trip

Below deck it felt like being crammed into a chicken pen, the 130 passenger boat was full to the brim and everybody was exitedly chatting and cackling on top of their voice. Definitely a great and positive atmosphere, but not something I'd enjoy for a full day! Luckily we were allowed to go outside after the boat sailed of, and only a hand full of people stayed there because of the cold and the wind, the rest disappeared below deck swiftly. I enjoyed the scenery on the way to the glacier very much. Beautiful light, a colony of cormorants, a spectacular waterfall spraying in the wind, and magnificent fjord and glacier landscape unfolding in front of the boat. They stopped the boat at points of interest, which allowed for time to have good looks and take photo's. Then the boat drops you off at land and you can walk to the glacier viewpoint. If you're a fast walker try to get off the boat first or you'll be as slow as the slowest person in front of you (Up to 130 persons, remember). Then at the viewpoint surely nice views, but I found it a bit underwhelming compared to other glaciers Ive seen in Patagonia. There was some pushing and shoving to take photos and selfies. Somebody accidentally knocked the lens cap of my camera without apologising, then a bit more crowd hassles, and back to the boat...that was it! Then onwards on the boat to the lunch stop at an estancia in a lovely location. The lunch was good, but the service was slowish and it took well over 2 hours. I wished I had the time to walk around and explore a bit around the estancia. maybe they should offer a quick lunch option to people who want to explore? Then back on the boat to Puerto Natales, again outside on the deck to avoid the crowds downstairs. And back to the hotel in a bus. Well organised, well executed, lovely staff, but a bit too much of a mass tourism thing to my tastes. And the crowdedness of it all caused moments which I experienced as awkward and unpleasant. I have noticed they also have smaller boats, and more exclusive trips, so please inquire. But on that day they crammed everyone on their biggest boat, which seemed to be the only one going there. I added some photo's of the lovely scenery, which was undeniably amazing!

review_text: Since we went to Atacama in the low season we thought it would not be a problem to book a stargazing tour. We read really good reviews for this company's tours and were shocked they told us they are already booked one week in advance. The problem is (and we did not know it beforehand) that they do not do tours a few days before and after the full moon because the moon's light obstructs the view of the stars. So make sure you come to Atacama on the right days if you want to do this tour. But fortunately the guy from the company massaged us a few days before that they have some spots open and we were super happy to be able to go on the tour on the last possible day before the moon got brighter. The whole experience is one of the best of all tours we did in Chile. Our Canadian guide was amazing, funny and knew so many fun facts about the stars. Also we could see he loves what he does and he was really prepared for us on that day because he showed us some things only visible for a few seconds on the night sky every once in a while (we saw the Hubble telescope which is super rare because it needs to be in the right angle to be visible). Even the stargazing with the naked eye was really interesting because the sky is so clear, so when we got to the telescopes we were amazed. The moon was so bright you could see the craters on it. Everybody that wanted got a picture of the moon through a special telescope that our guide took (event the worst cameras like mine on Sony telephone got a clear picture of the moon). Also we all fell in love with Saturn - it's rings were visible. At the end we all got some really good hot chocolate to get warm and got a chance to ask some questions about space. All in all a trip to remember. Highly recommendable!

First we had a lovely tour with Sam, one of the fellows there for the next year, who proved to be incredibly patient with our somewhat scattered group and was very knowledgeable about the grapes, wine, and history of the vineyard. He introduced us to Amael, the Kingston winemaker, who truly made us believe in the beauty and poetry that goes into the creation of this wine. He happily chatted with our group and told us all about the time and care that goes into their process and was wonderfully kind. We then moved on to possibly the most delicious lunch I've ever eaten - better than many 5-star gourmet restaurants I've been to - made by another one of the fellows, Alex (we're talking croquets, octopus, short ribs, chocolate tart, handcrafted ice cream and cherry sorbet... mouthwatering). Sam beautifully matched pairings with each course of the meal, and then took us up to the terrace for even more tastings. We finally got shown around the new kitchen and tasting room, which has an incredible view of the valley and up into the Andes off into the distance. The entire visit was absolutely amazing and was the highlight of our entire trip to Chile. They were incredibly welcoming and accommodating to both English and Spanish speakers. Would 100% recommend!! Hi Micaela, Thank you for visiting us at Kingston Family Vineyards. We're glad to hear that you had such a lovely afternoon with Sam and Alex!

review_text: We have done similar tours in many other cities. It is a good way of getting an overall feel of a place. This was our worst experience by some margin. First problem you cannot pay when you get on the bus. You have to go to one of the Turist offices which was not that easy to find. Second we arrived at the office about 3.15 pm wanting a day's ticket. Everywhere else we have been a day is 24 hours so we could have used the ticket until 3.15 the following day. Not in Santiago. If we bought a ticket then it would expire at 6 pm that day so to be able to use it the following day we had to pay for 2 days. One day cost 44,000 pesos for 2 persons (about £55) two days 60,000 pesos (£75) which we thought very expensive. Nevertheless we booked for 2 days. The bus was fine but on the seats my wife and I chose one of the sockets for the head sets did not work so I had to change seats. The commentary was poor and often out of sink with the journey. Whilst we did get to see quite a lot of areas of the city and the bus journey was pleasant, we really did not learn anything much about the city other than that it is vaste. review_text: What can I say about this man, Ismael, what a guy and what a superb week I had in November with him! He hosted me for most of the week in his log cabin that he built from scratch with his dog Lecce, I noticed on arrival that here there is no such thing as plaster and insulation. They use the old fashion plaster - mud! Amazingly, it was a very warm house. I enjoyed our adventures, we explored the wine valleys of Chile and tasted some of the expensive wines of the region, surfed every day as he taught me the fundamentals of ocean surfing and educated me on the Chilean way of life. Pichilemu and the people Ismael introduced me to have a different way of life than the ones I have met on my trip in Santiago. They are all about living their lives the best way possible. Currency is in favours in this part of the world and not nessessary money. In between surf trips Ismael would say 'before we go I have to drop off x', it may be compost, a drill bit, surfboard etc. Helping out your fellow neighbour in the town and somewhere down the line they will help you. He paid his mechanic a bottle of wine instead of currency to sort out an issue on his car. He spent most of the week apologising to everyone we met for not getting an invite to his wedding, a popular figure in the town. As a surf teacher, you will learn the fundamentals of ocean surfing, he is very patient and helps you develop your skills whether you are a natural or a beginner. Ismael also has plenty of surfboards and wetsuits (which is needed in the Pacific Ocean) so all equipment is taken care of. Evening time and going to a local bar where the price is much the same as the UK and this is a rural part of Chile, but the local was full until 3/4am with everyone enjoying themselves despite the price of the drink, the venue and the entertainment made the night. I was amazed to hear though that no-one wants to leave the area, it is beautiful and the positive atmosphere of the region I could understand why. I felt as I left on the bus that I escaped a Lotus Garden of the world as I could have stayed for much longer. Pichilemu is very much like the Hotel California - 'you can check out anytime you like, but you can never leave.' And I am sure you will feel the same too. Thank you Ismael and I hope we can meet again soon Highly recommend, Ismael will not disappoint!

In between surf trips Ismael would say 'before we go I have to drop off x', it may be compost, a drill bit, surfboard etc. Helping out your fellow neighbour in the town and somewhere down the line they will help you. He paid his mechanic a bottle of wine instead of currency to sort out an issue on his car. He spent most of the week apologising to everyone we met for not getting an invite to his wedding, a popular figure in the town. As a surf teacher, you will learn the fundamentals of ocean surfing, he is very patient and helps you develop your skills whether you are a natural or a beginner. Ismael also has plenty of surfboards and wetsuits (which is needed in the Pacific Ocean) so all equipment is taken care of. Evening time and going to a local bar where the price is much the same as the UK and this is a rural part of Chile, but the local was full until 3/4am with everyone enjoying themselves despite the price of the drink, the venue and the entertainment made the night. I was amazed to hear though that no-one wants to leave the area, it is beautiful and the positive atmosphere of the region I could understand why. I felt as I left on the bus that I escaped a Lotus Garden of the world as I could have stayed for much longer. Pichilemu is very much like the Hotel California - 'you can check out anytime you like, but you can never leave.' And I am sure you will feel the same too. Thank you Ismael and I hope we can meet again soon Highly recommend, Ismael will not disappoint!

review_text: Watch out for robbers in the Santiago airport in Chile We made arrangements for Transfer Santiago to pick us up at the airport in Chile. We were on time however when we left the terminal we could not see our name amongst the many taxi drivers holding signs. Suddenly this apparently “official” with a badge said that he could help us. He moved us away from the taxi drivers holding signs to another location. We had the paper info re our taxi pickup with the phone number. The “helper” called. My husband took out his phone to call but this one person kept giving us his phone to use. The other person on the line told my husband that it will take 3 hours until they could pick us up. My husband again wanted to use his own phone but this guy kept insisting to use his phone. We had a voucher for pick up so this man told us that we needed to get some money from the airport ATM in Chilean pesos to pay them so then we could get our voucher to get our refund. We were so tired and it all seemed to be in a dream. All we wanted was to get to our hotel. Well even though we had Chilean pesos they insisted that we use the ATM at the airport to get the money out to pay for their taxi and then we could be reimbursed. He provided a private transfer to the hotel. He showed a webpage with our hotel on it to verify the address. It showed a $146,00 peso charge - he said that was the cost. The cost that they showed is the charge for a night’s stay. He then charged 160,00 0pesos for the taxi ride!! He charged 160,000 pesos for a 20,000 per ride, 8 times the cost - CROOK!!!! It all sounded like a scam but we were so tired that we just wanted to get to our hotel. Well when we got home we found out that another 200,000 pesos was taken out from the ATM at the same time without our knowledge. So if you make arrangements for a taxi pick up just stay around until you see your pick up. In our case that pick up never showed up. We called the company and they insisted that their driver was there. Stay away from TRANSFER SANTIAGO. They even claimed that they had pictures to prove it.

review_text: My fiance and I did the Casablanca small group tour and a private tour to Valparaiso, both with Patricia as our guide. The Casablanca tour was full (so 8 people) and we had a fantastic day with the entire group. We visited at least a dozen vineyards in both Chile and Argentina during our trip and the first two vineyards we visited on this tour were my favorite of all of them (RE and Emiliana). The lunch was in a very elegant private dining room at a small boutique hotel - it was delicious but I was wishing for a nap after! Be ready for generous pours at all the tastings - I'll admit I only vaguely recall the last vineyard of the day. One piece of feedback is that bottled water in the van would have been good to help keep us going. The private tour to Valparaiso was also well done; upon request it included one vineyard stop on the way there to try a cold weather Malbec - it was nice way to start the day. We opted to do an early lunch (which for Americans means lunch at a normal time) in Vina del Mar. The lunch would be the one suggestion I have for improvement - it was at a fancy seafood restaurant with great view of the ocean so I get why we taken there, but it was pretty expensive and seemed to be a tourist trap given how many other tour groups were there. I would have much preferred somewhere that gave me an authentic Chilean experience and was filled with locals, even if it didn't have the view; so maybe that would be something to ask people preferences on beforehand. After lunch we got an overview of Valparaiso by car and then parked to continue exploring on foot. It came up during the day that it was my fiance's birthday so during a coffee break our guide surprised him with birthday waffles (complete with a candle)! It was a very nice touch that we both appreciated! Overall I would absolutely recommend Uncorked to friends and family visiting Santiago - great experience! Review of: Best Wine Tasting in Santiago

review_text: We did the w in three full days but skipped the French valley (so technically it's not the full w, but hey). You can go east to west or the other way around, but it should depend on the weather. If the weather is great, start east, otherwise you might miss the towers in the full glory. We did east to west. Some tips: - you have different choices to stay: refugios, which have to be booked (a lot of older people so this). Bring your own camping gear, rent it at hello Patagonia in Puerto Natales or rent your gear at the campsite in tdp. We rented it in Natales which is definitely the cheapest and best way to go, because you can stay at any campsite. The free campsites might be full, but they have no facilities. The private campsites are quite cheap and have showers, shops and bathrooms, which is a good option. - Bring enough money, better to have too much than too less. You might need 15k for the catamaran when you return. If you bring 100k it will suffice. - don't forget sunscreen!!!! You won't be able to buy it anywhere and you'll definitely need it.

review_text: Stayed at Casa Galos in Valparaiso for three nights following a cruise and the hotel recommended Waldo for a wine tasting day in Casablanca. The result was an extremely enjoyable day spent drinking wine in some of the most wonderful vineyards we have visitied either in the new or old world. Waldo was great throughout the day, relaxed knowledgeable and very safe despite some interesting road junctions to get to the vineyards. In total we visited four vineyards during the day,Emiliana Organic, Bodegas RE, Casas del Bosque and Kingston Family vineyards. The day started at Emiliana with a wine tasting of their premium wines and was so successful that we left with a bottle. All of the wines tasted were excellent and enjoyed in ideal conditions with no crowds and postcard views. We next moved onto Bodegas RE which was less successful as the vineyard appeared to be centered around organised tours during our visit so we did not have the opportunity to do a tasting or have a meaningful look around. Casas del Bosque is well known for its wine and restaurant and many people here were engaged in lunch upon our arrival. The food looked good however, and had we not been booked for lunch elsewhere it would have been pleasant to sample the dishes on offer. We were however able to sample a glass of wine taken in the garden amongst the vines something that proved to be a very enjoyable experience and we could have spent much longer here. With great good fortune our guide Waldo had recommended lunch at Kingston Family vineyard and we were not disappointed by the choice for it proved to be excellent. It is positioned in an elevated location providing outstanding views of the valley, absent from crowds of people and coach tours and blessed with excellent food and wine. We had a leisurely lunch with very enjoyable wines followed by a tour of the estate which ended a perfect day in Casablanca. If going to this area it is definitely worth getting away from the vineyards along the main highway as the rewards are well worth the extra time spent travelling and find a guide like Waldo. Thanks so much Stephen. The journey for the vinery was very nice and i now reading that the tour was very well for both, i feel proud and happy for your words Kind Regards!

review_text: Iliana the Chef met a nice young couple and myself promptly at 9 am and took us through an amazing tour of the multiple food, fish, flower, clothing markets around the Mercado central. Each market was fascinating and huge and fun to walk through. Absolutely be certain to wear good walking shoes. Once she assembled what we would need for our cooking lesson, we took a short subway ride to a lovely residential neighborhood and entered a lovely home, with a beautiful professional kitchen at the back. Over the next four hours, we made multiple fabulous dishes, all of it hands on direct experience. Iliana made certain that no one was idle. Apparently, she changes the menu at least monthly to reflect the current offerings. We started out making Dobladitas, the ubiquitous bread that we served as an Appetizer as we cooked with Pebrea, or Chilean Salsa. This put food in our bellies as we learned to make perfect Pisco sours. One could also have wines. We then made another course, called a Palta Cardenal, which was made with shrimps but for those of us who don’t eat seafood, mushrooms could easily be substituted and were delicious. The main course was a sesame encrusted Salmon served on a bed of past Leora, which was a fabulous mashed corn dish, as well as zucchini and tomatoes. I could not finish all of my food although the other couple was able to. We finished up with a chocolate encrusted panacota that was to die for. I am not certain that I will EVER be able to eat again. Wonderful introduction to Chilean food and wine. If one has any food allergies, can’t eat shellfish/pork, etc, just let the company know ahead and they will happily moderate. A great activity to add onto one’s schedule if one is in Santiago.

review_text: My husband and I arranged to climb this volcano with a local guide. While the guide was fantastic - I can't understate how difficult the climb was. We have "climbed" several (hiking / scrambling) mountains around the world and have also completed many multi-day treks, but an ascent of 1500 vertical meters over 6kms (12kms return - taking 10 hours) involving relentless volcanic scree and then snow/ice was way more physically and mentally exhausting than we realised. Not having ever climbed on snow/ice before, we were terrified the whole time of slipping and sliding down the mountain. In hindsight it probably wasn't quite as dangerous as it felt, but it certainly isn't easy and I would only recommend for the super fit and mentally strong. On the plus side - the views from Calbuco of Osorno and other surrounding volcanos is AMAZING. Volcan Calbuco itself is very interesting with its history of erruptions and the changes they have made to the mountain. Also, it was a real eye opener for us to get a taste of "real" mountain climbing using crampons, harnesses, ropes and poles etc. It wasn't for us but it might be for you!

review_text: We booked 5 tours with this agency, with the owner herself. When i realized 2 of the tours, booked for the same day clashed in schedule, she said it was our own fault. I asked for a refund, she said no. I booked the tour to the Lagunas Altiplanicas (high plateau lagoons) which are located at 4400 mts above sea level. The owner told us it was a slow climb up, stopping on the way, so no precautions were neccesary to avoid altitude sickness. We were taken straight , and quickly to the 4400 mts. People in our party felt sick. When I contacted the owner about this, she just said again, it was our own fault. She had also promised safe and comfortable transport. The minivan was missing the door handle on the inside, so the door could only be opened from the outside. When I asked about this, she said it was the fault of the German tourists who were always breaking the door handle. I am not german, but I found this extremely offensive and innapropriate. I ended up filing a complaint with the SERNATUR (Chilean National Tourism Agency), after which I got refunded for the tours I wasn't able to take because of schedule clashes and also with Carabineros de Chile (Chilean Police Force) for the lack of safety in her vehicles. She got fined for transporting passengers in unsafe conditions. The owner of this agency has no idea what customer service is, and she treated us rudely and with no respect whatsover..

review_text: I booked a 7-day tour with Jorge in November 23. 4 days in the Chilean Altiplano and 3 days in Bolivia. The booking with Altiplano Travel was a complete success and a lot of fun. Jorge is a walking encyclopaedia, he knows so much about the area, history and geology, he surprised me every day anew. My wish was to see places that are not overrun by tourists, Jorge took me to places where we were completely alone with hundreds of flamingos in a tremendous landscape. In addition, every day there was a fine meal with Chilean wine (I love Carmenere) in the most beautiful places. If you want to experience the Altiplano without being jammed into a horde of tourists, then book your tour with Jorge, you won't be disappointed. I was looking for a guide and found a friend. review_text: The first thing to highlight is that it was a perfect experience... I start by telling you that here you have the possibility of paying for a tasting before deciding on a wine, we arrived after 6 p.m. with the intention of buying wines and we were able to taste Garnacha and Petit Vedot. I must be honest, I did not buy quickly...the wines did not convince me, we had the option of doing the tour with tasting the next day and only because I found the plant attractive we booked it. We arrived the next day after 10am (the tour was at 10:30) and Nelson greeted us, indicating that everything was ready and we could start immediately, from then on it was very entertaining, Nelson is a native of the area and he tells you in living flesh the changes in the sector, and the effects on the people (I am quite a questioner). From there I was very grateful for the history and I find the history of this vineyard very inspiring, it flew by and the best came, a guided tasting with simple guidelines that one can replicate and with a game of senses that surprised me, we tried Malbec, Petit Vedot and "Family Edition", I loved the wines, they convinced me absolutely, the latter is a very well crafted red blend, this time I bought it... and I will definitely return, I had not had that feeling in the vineyards previously visited (Maquis and Viu Manent) so I stayed with these smaller vineyards, with very committed employees, here Nelson's passion stands out, which undoubtedly gave the experience the perfect accompaniment.

review_text: This was by far the highlight of our time in Santiago. Our guide, Gonzalo, was extremely knowledgeable and offered detailed and interesting information about the geology of the mountains, the history, and the animal and plant life. Luck was with us that day as we saw 4 condors!! His passion for the mountains and the environment was evident. There were only 4 in the group so our questions were answered and we all developed a friendship as we hiked. Oscar, our driver also accompanied us. Both were conscious of the pace and safety needs of each in the group. There were strategic stopping and resting points with unimaginable views. Lunch was in the shade of a giant rock. We were asked if we wanted to extend our hike and reach a place on the volcano. As one of the group did not wish to do this, Oscar returned to the starting point with the participant and the rest of us went further. We drank glacier water, saw more incredible vistas and He spoke in English and Spanish fluently and switched easily between the two. Out of the approximate 12 hours we only spent about 3 in the vehicle and that was to get to the base where we started the hike. Should we come back to Santiago we would do this hike again. So much to learn about the mountains and Chile! Many many thanks to Gonzalo and Oscar. Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo

review_text: I had the pleasure of taking a tour with Wild frames in Torres del Paine, and I can say without a doubt that it exceeded all my expectations. From the beginning, the team’s organization and professionalism were impeccable. The tour allowed us to delve into the majesty of the park, with landscapes that looked like they were taken from a dream. One of the most exciting moments was the sighting of cougars in their natural habitat, a magical encounter that I will hardly forget. In addition, the guide shared his vast knowledge about native fauna and flora, helping us identify species such as guanacos, cougars, condors and an impressive variety of birds. Native vegetation was also a sight in itself. We learned about the different plants that are part of the Patagonian ecosystem, with detailed explanations that made the walk even more enriching. The company’s attention to detail and commitment to environmental conservation really stood out. We make sure to follow sustainable practices throughout the tour, something I deeply appreciate as a conscious traveler. I would recommend this experience to anyone who wants to connect with nature in one of the most stunning places in the world. Thanks to Gaston and Carolina for an unforgettable experience!

review_text: In late March we used FSE and they did not tell us which guide we would have for a private birding tour. We were very disappointed in guide "Sebastian Saiter". He undoubtedly knows his birds, but has ZERO guiding skills. Don't pay for a driver and guide and have them talking to each other (in Spanish, which I understand btw) not spotting during the drive. We had to ASK that he take and use his scope, when we went looking for Magellanic Plover which we did not find. We had to ask for IDs on other birds that he would walk past, he did not brief us on where and what we would do, did not ask about our other trip locations (why scan virtually every flock of upland geese looking for ruddy-headed goose when we are going to the Falklands)?. On top of this, he showed up late and ended the tour early. Perhaps if he had actually spoken to us we might have had a more productive excursion. Many of the best birds were spotted first by us, or the driver! This tour was quite expensive, the lunch was canned tuna and cheap snacks, even that wasn't so good! I do not recommend using this company unless you are guaranteed a different guide. Another option is to just rent a car and drive to some of the ebird hotspots by yourselves, for all of the help we had. If you are coming off of a cruise ship there is little value added in birding along the Magellan Strait, as you will see nearly all of these birds elsewhere, especially if your guide doesn't want to visit bosques but focuses on checking every flock of upland geese for the likely-departed ruddy-headed goose (which you will see in abundance in the Falklands). Thankfully we had excellent guides out of Puerto Montt and Ushuaia. Still it felt like nearly $300 each down the drain. Dear Guest, I am very sorry to learn about your disappointment in relation with your experience with us in one of our day birding tours along the Straits of Magellan early this year. It's very hard for us and rest assured we will take measures in order to prevent things like this to happen in the future. Your reaction seems to be related with the insufficient guide performance which is surely the most important aspect of our product. Please accept our apologies. Respectfully, Claudio F Vidal and the FSE team.

review_text: We booked this tour after we arrived in Atacama after reading amazing reviews. I’m not sure if this tour company does not typically do tours in English, because when we got on the bus we realized the tour was only in Portuguese and we were a bit worried. Fortunately someone helped us to tell the guide, and arranged for us to go on a different tour in Spanish, but the tour guide also spoke English. We unfortunately cannot remember our tour guide’s name, but he was tall and had a pony tail, and his grandmother was from the town near Atacama. He was GREAT!! In addition to being able to translate everything to us in English, he made the tour really interesting. We learned about some cultural aspects of Atacama, along with a lot of geological information about the places we visited. But most importantly the guide shared really interesting and unique information about his family’s heritage from the surrounding area and it made the tour special. He also made us sit for a moment of silence and listen to the rocks, which was surprisingly meaningful. I think visiting both moon and Death Valley is a must. Note that the part of Moon Valkey tour is walking through a cave (beware if you are claustrophobic) and some climbing/ bending. The tour is mostly geological information and driving to sites, but still it’s probably best to do with a guide. The tour ends with a cocktail and meat, cheese, fruit desert at death valley. It was THE most beautiful place either of us had ever been. What a great experience! We wish we remembered our guide’s name!! Also he was amazing at taking pictures....

review_text: Sadly this is not a tour that will stand out as a highlight for us in our travels around South America. Not only was the Osorno volcano completely covered in cloud (and is apparently most of the time, as according to our guide, it rains approx 200 days a year there) but the Petrohue Waterfalls were also very crowded and there was only 15 mins allocated to our stay there which meant that we couldn't spend time walking the other trails and just had to stay on the main route. Puerto Varas is very scenic but due to the recent protests, a lot of shop windows were boarded up to prevent damage which spoils the charm of the place. We were given some free time to look around (not much to do there except window shop in the short time we had). During this time our guide was running around buying our lunch of empanadas and wine. The tour description described it as a lunch of traditional empanadas with either red or white wine on offer. I expected these to be eaten at a local restaurant but we ended up eating them sitting on a very damp brick wall (as it had just stopped raining) on the side of the road and there was only one bottle of red wine - no white wine on offer (we only drink white wine) and served in plastic disposable cups - clearly all bought from the supermarket there. Very amateurish and not what we were expecting. We then travelled through to Fruitillar and were given an hour and a half in a place where there is nothing to do. The museum is in Spanish and we found that most our group ended up finding a free wifi spot outside the theatre and so we all spent the time there downloading our messages and waiting for our guide and driver to meet up with us. Our guide was not great and could have given us so much more commentary taking us on a walking tour instead of leaving us with too much time there and yet so little time at the waterfalls. At one stage the sky cleared and we could see the top of the volcano but we wouldn't have even known to look there - it was just by coincidence - the guide showed no interest in us seeing it. There was no further commentary on the trip back to our cruise ship in Puerto Montt (about an hour away) and I felt the guide had lost interest. All our other tours with TripAdvisor in South America have been amazing so this was seriously disappointing. I wouldnt recommend it. Review of: Frutillar, Puerto Varas, and Petrohué Waterfalls Excursion from Puerto Montt Hi Beverly! We thank you for the time you took to write us. Here at GV Tours we take customer care very seriously. This is the first time Nelly has ever gotten a negative review, in fact she only has excellent reviews on TripAvisor, as tour guiding has been her life for 15 years. Regardless, I will take this review and give her feedback. Regarding your review, I am sure you are mistaken about the times as it is impossible to stay in Petrohue for 15 minutes as It takes a minimum of 50 minutes just to get to them and come back to the vehicle, and you mentioned you saw them. Please recall you did not order a vegetarian empanada beforehand, so the guide had to go out of her way to go to a cafe in the town Puerto Varas just so you may have something to eat during lunch. We had everyone else's empanada (beef) already in the vehicle. As you can double-check on our itinerary, lunch is picnic style and the place where we have lunch has been the same for many years,which is at the statue of Licarayen which is right on the shores of Llanquihue Lake and you can get a full panoramic view of the city. We also have lunch there because on a sunny day you are able to see the volcanoes right in front of you. We unfortunately can't do much about the weather or the windows being boarded up, and I am sorry you didn't notice that the museum had both English and Spanish descriptions, but again, we will make sure to take into consideration everything you have mentioned and thanks again for your time.

review_text: We enjoy art museums - especially when they are in historic buildings, so this made it onto our list of must sees while in Valparaiso. We were not disappointed. The collection is particularly concentrated in early 20th centry impressionism, but almost entirely from South American artists, which was refreshing and exciting, since we weren't very familiar with any of them, but loved the art. The building was even more interesting. It has been meticulously restored and many of the rooms have beautiful wood work and other ornamentation that is worth a visit all by itself. There is also a lovely garden to sit in and appears to be a coffee shop, though it was late in the day when we visited and the shop was closed. the climb to the museum is a little brutal, but interesting with the street art along the way. There is an ascensore which runs right to the museum, but it is being rebuilt at the moment and completely out of service. The view of the harbor and the the Plaza Sotomayor is also stunning from the garden. We thought this was clearly worth a couple of hours during our vist.

review_text: I can only confirm the previous reviews. Ascending South America's most active volcano was a huge life event for me and the kids. Initially my kids were reluctant but they were soon put at ease by the owner who explained what would happen and the safety measures. It is an all day event and you will be tired at the end of it. They took care that we were always happy and helped with kit if we were flagging, even when we were ready to give up, thus all of us making it to the top. The views from the crater on this clear day were unlimited and stunning in all directions. The descent can only be described as the best toboggan run/slide you will ever be on. As it is all snow, you put on a pair of trouser protectors and basically slide on your bum all the way down. This means you are not only having fun but you enjoy 30 mins of the most incredible view. review_text: I just returned yesterday from the 7 day Polar Circle trip with Antarctica XXI. We were scheduled to fly on Tuesday morning, 17 February. All 66 passengers anxiously awaited the news the evening before departure, and we were informed that we would not fly due to fog conditions at Frei Base on King George Island. We were all sorely disappointed, but the local staff did their best to calm nerves and keep us informed. The following day we received bad news again that we would not fly out due to continued bad weather. At that point nerves became frazzeled, and we all began to think about the tens of thousands of dollars we had spent on this trip to be stuck at an average hotel in Punta Arenas. Fortunately on the afternoon of 18 February we were told that we had a flight window and that we would attempt to fly out. We did eventually fly that afternoon and arrived on the ship at about 8pm the day after we were scheduled to arrive, therefore losing nearly 2 full days our of our 7 night journey. The crew on board did their utmost to ensure that we would still be able to experience the crossing of the Polar Circle, and they DID deliver that promise. Overall our experence on board was outstanding. The expedition staff and crew were wonderful, the service was excellent, and the excursions included landing the ship in ice and then walking out onto sea ice to celebrate with a glass of champagne, a barbeque on the top deck including dancing south of the Polar Circle, and a glacier walk which was incredible. We arrived back in Punta Arenas last night satisifed and delighted with our experience having seen a host of wildlife and natural beauty. A word of CAUTION to all propsective passengers - weather delays are REAL and do occur. The Company is very clear regarding contingency plans in case of weather - they are honest and upfront about that from the day you make your first deposit. Simply do not assume it can never happen, because it does. Overall the experience of Antarctica was amazing, but be aware that the trip can be delayed due to weather which is beyond anyone´s control. As a single traveler, I paid nearly $21,000 for this trip, and despite the loss of two days due to weather, it was still a worthwhile investment. One important reminder that the Company does not make clear upfront - be sure to bring trekking poles for the glacier and sea ice walking. Those who did not have them or rent them on board were at a disadvantage.

review_text: Housed in a former Royal Courthouse built early 1800s during colonial times, the museum offers an overview of the history of Chile until the military coup in 1973. Better than similar museums in Latin America e.g. the one in Buenas Aires, but this one as well does not pay a lot of attention to what happened during the Conquista (1540 - 1600). How big was the resistance of the native population? What happened to them after defeat in the major battles? Emphasis is very much on the generals and their military achievements. Still worth while to visit and get at least one perspective on the national history.

review_text: Nice, safe area to take a stroll for a few hours, window shopping in the various "galerias" (buildings with their doors open, which contain a number of small stores...definitely go in and have a look around!). The majority of stores in this sector are of the furniture, design variety, but there are also clothing, jewellery and bookstores. Numerous cafes here as well, both on the street and inside the galerias. Great place to take pictures as the exteriors and interiors of many of the buildings are tastefully decorated. I'd say this area is worth exploring for those who have already seen a lot of other attractions in Santiago, but wouldn't recommend it for tourists with limited time. Directions: Take the subway to Santa Isabel (line 5), take the Oriente exit and turn left on Santa Isabel street. Walk about 10min until you get to Italia. Turn right on Italia and you'll start seeing the numerous galerias.

review_text: We booked a city tour of Santiago with Paseos en Bicicleta for Saturday, August 7, 2010. Prior to our tour, Andres contacted me to ask about the interests of our five year old son, nine year old daughter, my husband, and me. I told him our son loved trains, our daughter enjoyed art, my husband was into history, and I was most interested in Chilean politics and culture. To my surprise and great pleasure, Andres created a customized tour for us based on our interests. Our biking tour included an outdoor steam train museum which we all loved; we had an option for an interactive children's museum; Ines provided an incredibly detailed description of the founding of Santiago, Chilean literature, global warming, the impact of earthquakes on the city over the last few centuries, and how immigration has affected the Chileans - and other topics, as she is an encyclopedia of knowledge; and Andres not only organized and led the tour but also described in detail the psychology of the Chilean people in the environment of the changing Chilean government over the last forty years, answering every last question we asked. As the political discussion with Andres was becoming very involved at lunch, Karole - who is a teacher - took it upon herself to entertain our children with some toys she had brought, allowing us to immerse ourselves totally in our conversation. Our planned tour of five hours stretched to eight, and we would have been honored to continue our conversations over dinner [we'll have to save that for our next trip to Santiago!]. The biking was great fun, but the best part of a bike tour with Andres, Ines, and Karole is getting acquainted with some good-hearted Chileans, and to gain some understanding of the mindset and lives of Chilean people, Chilean history, and how they have evolved to become the magnificant country of Chile in 2010.

review_text: My two friends and I traveled to Santiago for a girls trip. After looking at a lot of different options online, I decided on this tour even though it was fairly new. Our tour guide, Frank and our driver picked us up at our AirBnB in Santiago the time they said that they would. We ended up being the only ones taking the tour that day so it was a very personal experience. Frank grew up in the States and spoke excellent English. He was very amiable and easy to talk to. He explained a lot about wine-making as well as Chilean culture, customs and Chilean-Spanish slang. All three of the wineries were great. At the first tasting, the winery tour guide actually taught us how to do a wine tasting which was needed because I had never been to one before. The wine portions at all 3 wineries were very generous so you need to make sure to keep drinking plenty of water throughout the day. Some of the tour was in Spanish which was fine for us but English translation is also available. The stop for lunch was delicious and we were able to order some wine that we had enjoyed at the previous winery. The price of lunch is not included in the tour but it was very reasonable; probably around $8-14 depending on what you order. Because of the time we spent at lunch, we arrived late to our third winery tour which made us rush around the vineyard trying to find a group to join. We did find a group and didn't miss too much of the full tour. Overall, this was a fantastic experience. We felt completely safe and learned so much. The one thing I would've done different is I would've eaten a more substantial breakfast and brought snacks to eat in between wineries because they give you a LOT of wine to taste. Make sure to bring a water bottle too. Review of: Maipo Valley Wine Tour with 4 vineyards from Santiago.

review_text: The first indication that one is near La Chascona is the mural, aptly enough, showing a redheaded woman riding a bicycle directly across the street. The house itself is an eclectic blend of odd things. However, the intimate neighborhood surrounding, proximity to the base of Cerro San Cristobal, zoological garden and other attractions make it a very close place to visit. The docents were finally able to answer the perennial question - how was it that Neruda had 3 "wives" without evidence of divorces which were prohibited in Chile until 2004....by explaining the use of annulments. The interior garden, the multiple levels of housing and opportunities for entertaining, I think, gave one additional insight into the author's life and effect on everyday Chilenos.

review_text: Veronique was our teacher/chef for the evening. We started off by agreeing on a menu after discussing any allergies, food intolerance or other food limitations. We were a group of 4 so the negotiating was easy. Although the group voted for making a dish with gluten in it, and I have celiac disease, Veronique engineered a different dish for me ensuing that I didn't have to skip anything AND that everyone else got their first choice. Having chosen our menu it was off to the food market, bakery, frozen food store, grocery and butcher which was lots of fun. Along the way we learn a lot about life in Santiago and got to ride the trolley. Once off the trolley, it was uphill to the hostel where the kitchen is located. If someone finds walking up or down hill a problem, this could be a detraction. For us it was fine - and even welcome after all the food! Cooking together was fun and there was plenty of water, wine and pisco sours, snacks and the many dishes we made. Everyone did chopping, kneading, stirring etc. and we all learned about each other during the class. All in all a great evening.

review_text: Note: this tour company is most suitable for older people and those who don’t like a lot of walking. It’s mostly a bus tour. TurisTours runs a range of Tours from Santiago. These include some to the Andes, Farellones Snow Park, Valle Nevado, Cajon del Maipo and El Yeso Dam, Vina del Mar and Valparaiso as well as wine tours and a general city tour. We selected the Vina Del Mar and Valparaiso tour for $36 000 CHP. We were collected at 8am for ‪a 9 am‬ tour. We drove around to pick up other guests and reached a central location where we all swapped buses for the relevant tour. Our bus was a small mini bus but there were larger ones depending on the tour. Our tour Included a bilingual guide. Most people were Spanish so he primarily spoke Spanish and translated for us. On the drive down the bus driver commentated on what we were passing with a lot of detailed knowledge. Unfortunately due to the public holiday, the winery was closed and we couldn’t visit it. This tour included a trip to Vina del Mar, known for its green surroundings and gardens in an urban city. There’s a visit to the famous Flower Clock, it’s a fairly uneventful visit. Take a photo and get back on the bus. The same at a few other spots like a beach and to see some sea lions. We then drove through the city and were explained things. We would have liked a look around. We were taken to a restaurant and offered ala carte or the special “tour company “ lunch. We went in and It was expensive (and the waitress was incredibly rude), so we chose to leave eat and at a cheaper excellent restaurant across the road at D’Lamari. We highly recommend doing this. The bus travels along the pacific coast to Valparaiso, Chile’s main port. This city is also a heritage site selected by UNESCO. Here we stopped for some more photos. This was better as we did a 1 hour walk through the Multi-coloured neighbourhoods and caught the Furnicular down. We would have liked to look more here. There was the offer of a boat ride (which minimum 8 people needed to do) at an extra cost but our group weren’t keen. We had 30 minutes to look around and then headed back to the city and dropped at our hotel. Brochure said bus has wi fi, which it didn’t. We personally found this extremely expensive for what you get. We also found it pretty boring - it’s a bus tour. We would prefer to look around. So do your research to make sure it’s your thing. You can do this cheaper by catching a local bus, but we had limited time and felt like a tour was easiest for us. That said we wouldn’t book these sort of things again. On a positive note, Martin was outstanding. Knowledgeable and funny. Dear Guest We appreciate that you have chosen Chile and that you have decided to take the Tour to Viña del Mar and Valparaíso. Thanks for your congratulations to Martín, we know he is a great guide and we will share your comments with him. We appreciate the tips that you are sharing with the tourists, indeed we go to a restaurant where there is a special TurisTour menu and everyone its free to decide if they want to eat that fixed Menu or a la Carte or even you can go and look for another options in the area, unlike other tour companies that take you to places where there is no where to choose. We deeply regret that the tour did not meet your expectations and we will undoubtedly take your appreciations to improve. Perhaps a more suitable tour for you would be a private tour in Valparaiso or as you said, just explore the city on your own without taking a tour. Regarding to the appreciation of the value of our regular tour ( S.I.B), just to let you know our rates are fair compared to other companies that offer the same service. We are a legal company, that pays taxes , ensurences and the tour guide and driver deserve a fair payment for a Full Day Tour. Thanks again and if you want to share more comments, please feel free to contact me cgaldames@turistour.cl

review_text: I spent a lovely afternoon at what must certainly be among the world's pre-eminent museums on precolumbian culture. Recently renovated and reflecting the immense gains in scholarship of this era made in the past two decades, the museum takes visitors on a journey into Latin America's rich pre-Columbian history. Visitors can download an app that allows independent "guided" tours, with commentary that will satisfy the curiosity of those interested in learning more. The fantastic artifacts and exhibits are well staged and lit. And when the treasures become overwhelming, there is a lovely inner courtyard where one can grab a tasty bite to eat and absorb discoveries. A must for any and all history buffs and those interested in Latin America's "real" history!

review_text: What a great day. We took the cycling tour at Santa Rita vineyard and it could not have been better organised. The pick up from the hote was efficient and in a new and comfortable vehicle. We stopped at La Bicicleta's depot on the way out of town, picked up the bikes and our charming host Liz. The journey was relatively quick and once there we stopped for a coffee and tasty empanada before getting on our bikes and cycling to Santa Rita. The bikes were in excellent condition and well maintained. Next we had a leisurely 2 hours touring the vineyards with regular stops at which Liz explained what we were seeing. Liz is very knowledgeable and had us captivated with her stories and information. It felt more like having a morning out with a friend than a tour guide. Having worked up a thirst we headed to the Casa, where we sat in the beautiful garden and enjoyed a glass of white while we waited for our tour guide from the winery. Next was the tour - again a wonderful host, with an easy relaxed style but all the information we could ever want, The tour culminated with a tasting in the historic cellar. This was accompanied by some excellent cheese and biscuits. As a bonus, because we had had to wait for a few minutes for an English speaking guide, we were treated to three additional 'iconic' wines that aren't usually available for tasting. On completion of tasting we had an opportunity to shop for wine, drove ( too many wines for safe cycling) back t the breakfast restaurant and had an excellent wine accompanied by another local wine. All in all a perfect day out. I cannot speak highly enough of the professionalism and courtesy we experienced. Highly recommended. Holaaaa Alister S We should get you to write the description of the tour for our web page, a perfect description of what we intend Santa Rita to be for people! Thank you so much for your kind words about our tour, Liz you're guide and our bikes. It's great to hear such positive feedback on the hard work we have put in over the last eight years. We live for travelers positive experiance over anything else we do here. I hope you enjoyed the rest of you're stay here in our beloved Chile (i'm sure you slept well after out on the bikes and sun with plenty of wine). Safe travels where ever you are headed too, and don't forget to swing by and say hey to the green gurus if you are ever back in town! Gracias, Peter.

review_text: We did 2 day tours with Ecochile during our 5 day stay in Santiago: snow hike in Cajón de Maipo and Valparaíso and wines. In the first, we (my partner and I) had a great day walking for around 13/14 km through the Andes mountains until and up in the San José volcano. Our guide Alejandro was excellent, friendly, knew the spot very well and did everything in his power to fit the tour to our wishes. He also gave us a referral for an excellent trekking guide in Atacama. The trekking is a little demanding, so be prepared. But the views and the activity itself are great and well worth the effort. In the second tour, we went to Viña del Mar for a quick overview (we previously asked for that), then spent a few hours walking around the vibrant Valparaíso, and ended the tour with a tour and wine tasting in Emiliana winery. Our guide Javiera was also friendly and knowledgeable about both cities. The winery was a nice end to the tour. Out guide there, Josie, was sweet, and the wines we proved (with different types of cheese and chocolate) were good. Since it was our first time in Chile, we wanted to see Viña del Mar, but for a second visit I would skip it and spend more time hanging around in Valparaíso. One can hire far cheaper tours in Santiago, but I doubt with the same level of service (and experience) that Ecochile provides. One last word: we paid the full price over a month in advance. review_text: Whilst visiting family in Santiago November 2016 we decided to visit Villarrica, Pucon for a 4 days to take in some of the scenery. If like me you live in the UK the best way I can describe Pucon is the Lake District x100. Pucon is where People from Santiago take their holidays and it's easy to see why! We visited in off peak season so the area was pretty quiet and decided we would take a day trip up to the volcano. Before travelling to Chile we had the volcano's and caves on our list of things to do but were quickly told by the locals in Santiago that after a recent eruption, the caves were now closed. We were slightly disappointed about this but went to visit the volcano none the less! Whilst on the way, we seen a sign fir the caves so decided to drive towards it. We came to a booth with a cone in the road where we assumed you use to pay. It looked like no one had been there in years and was surrounded by abandoned construction equipment. Just as we were about to turn around a man approached the car and assured us the caves were still open but he was in the process of clearing the mess the eruption had left behind. The young man asked for 18,000 chilean peso each which we thought was quite expensive especially for this part of the country but paid the man none the less. We were taken up a trail to a small Cafe with great views of both the volcano and the sea. The young chilean didn't really speak english but my father-in-law spoke basic spanish so between them we managed. The information that we did manage to understand was good and although there was a slight language barrier the young chilean did his best. The Tour lasted about 20 mins before we had to turn around and come back. Hard hats were supplied as there are areas that are as low as 5 foot. The tour guide then told us in the nicest way possible that he was finished his shift and would have to take us back! Overall, it didn't feel very well organised. If you don't speak spanish or have someone to translate there isn't much point taking this tour especially at 18,000 peso. The tour isn't suitable for the elderly or children as like most South American countries, the health and safety is basically nonexistent. I wouldn't recommend you travel all the way just for this tour but if you're in the area or are really into exploring caves then it might be for you.

review_text: Firstly, the actual vineyard tour, tasting wine and cheese led by Concho y Toro employees was VERY GOOD, 5 out of 5. The actual tour operator that picked us up charged a huge amount, I understand profit, but!!! In our 2 months in South America, we did dozens of tours, so im a fairly good judge of tour operators and their guides, in fact I'm a retired travel agent and tour guide. The young man who picked us up from our hotel, showed us the motor coach door and said welcome was one of only 2 tour guides who was totally hopeless (possibly nobody has trained him in what a tourist expects for the money they pay!!?) We circled round the city and picked up a full bus load from various hotels. Once all aboard there was no welcome speech, possibly adding us where we were all from, it was more like a public bus, not a coach tour. His Englush was okay, a bit difficult to understand, obviously Spanish was his first language, but we did pay for an English tour. En route to the vineyard there was a dozen things that the guide could have mentioned in passing even if the vineyard was the actual destination. On arrival at the vineyard the guide told us where bathrooms were, he then went across to the ticket office to buy our tickets. We crowded round him to get our wristbands and he gave the Portuguese passengers theirs and told us English speaking folk that someone called Christian (I think) had Ours. Who the heck is Christian was the first thing everyone asked, it turned out he was our tour coach driver, gee pity we hadn't been introduced. Then we found out that was rhe end of the guide's duties. He showed us where the vineyard tour guides were and explained that the English speaking tour would leave in a little over an hour. Portuguese speakers went immediately then had to wait for us at the end. Our bus tour guide could learn a huge amount about guiding if he accompanied Phillipe from the vineyard, he was the ultimate tour guide! 2 Norwegian passengers through a complete hissy fit right about this time and I have no idea how the bus tour guide dealt with them but from personal experience I think he would have been way out of his depth. At the end of an excellent vineyard tour we piled on the bus to return to the city Not once did this tour guide get off the bus to say goodbye or thank us. In fact he was busy talking to the driver when we got off and never even acknowledged we'd got off. Obviously no tip, we decided we'd spend our USD tip on some more wine at our hotel bar. Pity the driver missed out too! review_text: PLEASE DO NOT BOOK WITH THIS COMPANY AND READ MY REASONS BELOW... I booked a tour with Sol y Nieve to climb Volcano Villarica. My friend and I were given an explanation of the tour the day before. The explanation was good except for the manager swearing every 5 sentences - we didn't mind but still thought this was not professional. The day started off well. I was at the front of the 'slower' group and keeping pace with our allocated guide quite comfortably. We reached the midway point and I was told to stop by my guide. He permitted the two people behind me to continue but told me to stop - NO reason was given but since he was the professional, I obeyed. After about 10 minutes of watching the rest of my group continue with their climb, I asked my guide what we were waiting for. It was only then that he communicated to me that I couldn't continue anymore because it was 'too dangerous'. I was shocked as I was given NO reason by my guide and I had to provoke this out of him. Another guide told me I was too slow and for my safety I could not carry on. I argued how I was slow? I was walking at the pace of which my guide was setting with two others walking behind me, who were themselves permitted, and could've increased the pace if I needed to. I was not asked if I wanted to continue, I had no choice in the matter. I wasn't even told I was slow and asked to pick up the pace or that we were running late? I started to walk to chase after my group but was informed that by now it was too late. I then had to wait 4 hours whilst the rest of my group made it to the top and returned. Upon their return I discovered that the guides who had gone with them had said on multiple occasions that they were moving incredibly quickly and we arrived earlier than expected which meant that considering I was keeping pace before, I WASNT slow and could've caught up! Nobody could understand in my group why I was stopped. I complained to the manager, Willy, who was incredibly rude and disrespectful to me... Possibly because of the beer he was holding in his hand. I initially requested to speak to him in private to which he agreed but then walked away from me. I asked him again for his time and mentioned that I was not happy about the way I was treated. He immediately got defensive and said 'well I wasn't there on the mountain so can't say much'. This was BEFORE I had even started to discuss anything with him. Willy then called the guide that I was with and asked for his account first. It then transpired that I was stopped as I was breathing heavily. I am asthmatic but have no issues with trekking seeing as how I have already done tours like the Inca Trail in Peru, Laguna 69 and lake churrup in Huaraz and Chacaltaya in Bolivia - all higher than Villarica. I had even told a member of their staff the day before that I'm asthmatic and will breathe heavily and was told this wasn't an issue. Willy again started to get defensive and said we should've told the guides - maybe I should have but they should've asked about physical conditions of the people in their group - where is the health and safety elements?? In addition to this they at least should have told me WHY I was being stopped in the first place then I could've explained straight away. It also meant I was initially lied to because it wasn't because I was 'too slow' at all. Willy refused to let me say my side of the incident and kept interrupting me to speak to the other guides in Spanish. They all were evidently talking about me and in front me - one even mentioned in English 'no physical condition'. I'm a size 14 female and thought that was very presumptuous and offensive - especially as I've had no issues hiking in higher altitudes in the past which I also mentioned to the manager the day before in passing. At this point, two other independent tourists who were also in my group (one of which who was behind me in the first half of the climb) even felt they needed to step in and corroborate my story... Willy still didn't want to listen to them either. After all if this I said I wanted compensation. I was offered to go on a canopy or rafting tour instead (which is worth less than 1/3 of what I paid for the Villarica tour). I politely but honestly declined and said I wouldn't like to participate in any more tours with this company and that I would like my money back. The response was a laugh from Willy saying 'well it's a free country and you can do whatever the hell you want' and refused to give any money back. After some more debate, Willy finally and reluctantly agreed to give half my money back. He then realised that since I had paid by card then he will have incurred a % fee for me using the card and then started to complain how he would lose out more because of that - which isn't my problem. I had travelled to Pucon to specifically climb this volcano but was instead left feeling incredibly frustrated and insulted. The company may have received good reviews on here before but that's because they didn't have a run in with the manager. A completely unprofessional company who doesn't understand the concept of 'the customer is always right'. We are extremely sorry to hear you suggest not to book with Sol y Nieve. We believe our other fantastic reviews speak for themselves and reach out to our future clients to take them all into account instead of just yours. Our guides are trained to make a call on whether someone can achieve the summit in the time period alloted to all groups. Your guide made the decision that you would not reach the summit before 2pm based on the firrst part of the climb. This time allotment is a requirement which must be complied with by all agencies taking clients to the crater since the re-opening of the volcano in November 2015. The owner of Sol y Nieve compensated you for your disappointment so we would like to close by wishing you an enjoyable stay in Chile for the duration of your trip.

review_text: This day out from Santiago was a great way to end my time in Chile as it's a nice and easy way to spend a day. The bus was fairly comfortable compared to other buses I've been on. Cata was a great and personable guide who brought energy to the group and showed nice personal interest in each of the participants. The first stop on the tour was likely my favorite. The passion and energy of the guide (forgot his name) as he explains the winery's process was great. There are also animals to see here and some wines & Pisco to try which are served along with snacks. There are also products available to buy at fair prices. The second winery had nice wines but the tour aspect was a bit hastily done. It did have beautiful surroundings though and a chance to try some local fruit growing on the trees. The third stop for lunch was very nice and everyone enjoyed their food. The last stop also was nice and the surroundings are absolutely gorgeous. I also enjoyed the tour through their facilities. You can also taste some of the grapes here as well as the wines. If you can do this tour with a group a friends or family, it would be great as it's very social considering the aspect of sharing drinks and food together. Even travelling alone however, it was a pleasant experience as we had a lively group where people interacted well with each other and with the guides. Overall, I really recommend this tour if you want to get a nice overview of some of the region's wine making or just spend a nice day experiencing great food & drink.
